subject: fennec
pitch: A fennec fox kit standing alert on a little sand dune at dusk. Enormous satin ears lined in pale peach, cream fur warming to sandy gold along its back, a fluffy tail with a smudge of black at the tip, and big dark eyes with a tiny white sparkle. Its paws are a touch oversized, like it hasn't grown into them yet, and it wears a woven leather collar with a small brass bell.

Now I'm working out the joint hierarchy and coordinate placement, building a hips root joint with a spine chain curving up to the chest, positioned relative to the dune's height.

Defining joints and chains...

For the spine, I'll just use joints named "spine1" and "chest" with no separate tip. For the head, the tip joint gets its orientation from the tangent along the neck path.

I'm working out the coloring too — outer ear in cream, inner lining in a peach tone, likely as two separate extruded layers (outer cream shell plus a thinner peach lining sitting slightly in front) instead of a complex gradient paint function.

Still working out ear geometry...

I realize the broad face of the ear should face forward since that's the view seen from the front of the fox, so I need the plate's normal to point along +Z, meaning the ear's local axes should use lateral X for width and vertical Y for height rather than the orientation I was considering.

For coloring, I decide the inner lining (facing +Z, toward the viewer) should be peach while the outer back face (-Z) is cream, since that matches how fennec ears look from the front with the tilt applied.

Now for the tail, I'm planning a fluffy curved chain of bones from the hips that sweeps backward and up, with a radius function that bulges thicker in the middle and tapers near the tip, colored sandy-cream gradually fading to black at the very tip.

For the body, I'm sweeping along a spine chain from hips to chest with a radius profile that's slightly wider than tall, growing gradually toward the chest to give the torso an elongated, rounded shape with default round caps.

For the neck, I'll sweep a shorter chain connecting spine to head with a roughly constant thin radius, tapering slightly toward the head joint.

For the head, I'm planning to use a loft across several stations—muzzle tip, snout, cheek, and back of skull—each with its own width and height to build the wedge-shaped fox skull, using the loft's bone binding to tie it to the head joint for weighting.

Adding a small nose-tip sphere rigged rigidly to the head bone, then setting up a countershade gradient from sandy gold on the back to cream on the belly for the fox's fur, applied across body and head based on surface normal direction. Now I'm moving on to the eyes, placing dark spheres with a bright sparkle highlight at symmetric positions on the face.

For positioning the eyes precisely on the curved skull surface, I'm using a surface query against the head loft mesh to find the nearest point and normal at the target location, then sticking the eye geometry onto that hit frame with a slight embed so it seats naturally into the face rather than floating. I'm also double-checking that the loft sweep used for the head has its fill color properly specified since that option is required for the sweep to render correctly.

For the ears, I'm calculating where the base should sit on top of the skull by estimating the loft's peak height and lateral position, then using the same surface-nearest technique to get a hit frame there, which I can feed directly into the ear extrusion as the attachment point.

For the ear coloring, I'm defining a paint function that checks the surface normal's z-component to decide between peach (inner, front-facing) and cream (outer, back-facing) tones, which should naturally highlight the inner ear.

Now I'm planning the legs for the fennec kit with oversized paws, deciding to build each leg as a chain of points running from hip or shoulder down through knee/ankle to paw tip, figuring out approximate coordinates for the front and hind limbs.
